correctness.rationale: Checked the narrower final RESULT and the original proof independently. The palette reduction can be realized by mapping each block of discarded clusters to the retained cluster at its right end, preserving colors. Every predecessor sees the representatives of its own and each later block and no earlier block, so this is a bounded morphism. In the reduced chain consecutive supports fail inclusion; inducting from the right, a newly added color outside the leading old palette can see a type unique to that old leading block while no old world of that color can. Access to the resulting new type distinguishes all other new-block colors from old types. The finite quotient classes are the Boolean atoms. For iid colors, a specified support has probability p_j and the hold probability from size j is (j/q)^r. Appending clusters on the left preserves the existing suffix quotient contributions and gives exactly the joint polynomial recursion. A full palette exists with positive probability iff r≥q, and the first such palette bounds the limit by q times a geometric waiting time. Below saturation, a singleton outside the current support connects to any support not directly reachable; the finite chain is irreducible with holding. Stationarity for each specified j-support yields the displayed triangular recurrence by separating its own mass from strict supersets. The reward is a function of consecutive states, so its finite-state ergodic average is the stationary expected reward. The conditional subtraction j[(j/q)^r−((j−1)/q)^r] counts colors only on the hold event. This yields positive rational mu, with weights 1/7 and 6/7 and rewards 27/16 and 22/16 at q=4,r=2, giving 159/112. At r=1 the formula reduces to the known rate 1−1/q. Inspected the frozen finite checker, not executed; the proof, not finite checks, establishes the limiting claims.

originality.rationale: This is a PASS for the revised claim only. The original Finding promoted the exact deterministic support reduction, and the originality rationale failed to credit direct prior coverage; that part of the original originality decision fails. The October 12 canonical palette-word normal form already supplies exactly that reduction and atom count, and the October 26 reflexive-chain result also already covers the r=1 random case. The complete revised RESULT, SLOGAN, REVIEW and scientific audit comparison under the repair ordinal credit those results and narrow the finding to the clustered probability law and fixed-r growth, especially the exact finite recursion and the triangular formula for the positive stationary coefficient. In the known reduction, full-support absorption is an immediate structural consequence, not a separate new modal theorem. The inspected earlier results do not supply the joint finite law and all-parameter stationary reward calculation together for these ordered random clusters.
